title: Client Priority Credits and Sprint Reservation Protocol
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem statement: Strategic customers frequently request expedited delivery or guaranteed capacity for critical launches. Current intake uses ad-hoc emails and lookup tables, causing unclear commitments, sprint churn, and unfair prioritization. This ticket proposes a formal "priority credits" system where top accounts earn or purchase credits that can be redeemed to reserve sprint capacity, request fast-track engineering support, or trigger an escalation lane. The protocol includes allocation rules, reservation lifecycle, guardrails for rollback, and billing/accounting hooks.
goals: Create a deterministic priority allocation that scales across 100+ top accounts
Reduce ad-hoc escalations that cause sprint churn by 60% within two quarters
Provide transparent accounting so sales and finance can reconcile reserved work to contracts
Ship a minimal UI + API for assigning/redeeming credits and viewing reservations
success_metrics: Percent of escalations routed through the credits flow >= 80% after Q1 launch
Sprint churn (stories moved in/out within two-week cycle) reduced by 60% for accounts using credits
Time-to-commit for priority requests median <= 3 business days
Finance reconciliation accuracy to within +/- 3% of billed reserved capacity
proposed_solution: Design a credits ledger and reservation primitive: (1) Credits issuance: accounts receive a baseline allocation each quarter based on contract tier + one-time grant for strategic events; (2) Redemption: credits are consumed to create a 'reservation' indicating scope, desired sprint window, and acceptance criteria; (3) Guardrails: per-cycle reservation cap, cooldown period, and automatic rollback if acceptance criteria are not met or engineering capacity SLA is violated; (4) Visibility: Console view for Customer Success, Sales, and Eng to see active reservations and credit balance; (5) Billing integration: credits can map to pre-paid contractual credits or show as invoice events for managed purchases.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (design & spec, 2 weeks): finalize allocation algorithm, reservation lifecycle, and API contract
Phase 2 (backend + ledger, 3 sprints): implement credits ledger, reservation APIs, basic guardrails, and DB schema
Phase 3 (console + API docs, 2 sprints): UI for CSMs + accounts, SDK updates, and billing hooks
Phase 4 (pilot, 4 weeks): run with 8 strategic accounts (mix of Hosted, Dedicated, Private) and collect metrics
Phase 5 (iterate & scale): address feedback, add automation for auto-acceptance heuristics and cross-account fairness rules
acceptance_criteria: Credits ledger persists issuance/redemption events with idempotency and audit trail
Reservation API supports create/read/update/cancel and enforces per-cycle caps
Console shows real-time balances for scoped user roles and a reservations timeline
Pilot customers can redeem credits and receive an acknowledged reservation within SLA
Billing emits reconciliation records for redeemed paid credits
risks: Accounts may game the system by aggregating micro-requests; need scope definition and acceptance criteria to avoid abuse
Billing complexity if credits are both pre-paid and used as contractual commitments
Engineering capacity modeling may be inaccurate; reservations could lead to overcommit and SLA violations
Inter-team coordination: console, billing, and runtime teams need aligned product contracts
Security: audit trail must be tamper-evident for enterprise customers (may later require HSM-backed signing)
open_questions: Should credits auto-expire at quarter end or roll into a reduced carryover cap?
Do we permit partial-redemption for multi-sprint projects or require discrete reservations per sprint?
Is redemption capped to feature-level acceptance criteria or can it reserve non-functional work (capacity tuning, infra)?
How should credits map to Dedicated capacity reservations (do we reserve GPU pools or engineering effort)?
Do we expose an API for partners to programmatically redeem credits via CI/CD triggers?
